title: 50℃的浓缩，倒进0℃的牛奶 | What Makes a Dirty Coffee ☕
description:
你喝 dirty，会先拍照还是先喝？评论区告诉我。

一杯 dirty，是把滚烫的浓缩直接浇进冰牛奶里——不搅拌，任由深色的咖啡自己在纯白牛奶里晕开，黑白交界像打翻的墨，「脏」这个名字就是这么来的。它的源头在东京：2009 年回到东京的田中胜幸开出 Bear Pond Espresso，这杯最早就叫「The Dirty」。喝法也有讲究：第一口几乎全是浓缩的醇苦，最后一口回到奶的清甜——一杯咖啡，两种心情。

A "dirty" is hot, strong espresso poured straight over ice-cold milk — no stirring, so the dark coffee bleeds down through the pure white milk, leaving a messy black-and-white look that gives the drink its name. It traces back to Tokyo's Bear Pond Espresso, opened by Katsuyuki Tanaka in 2009, where it was simply called "The Dirty." First sip: bold espresso. Last sip: sweet milk.

Facts only, no endorsement. AI-assisted edit; the subtitles are the narration — no voiceover. Footage licensed from Pexels (credited below).
